I don't really care for superhero movies. I want to; how great would it be to be into the fad these days, multi-million dollar blockbusters that suit my interests to a tee. Well, they don't. I know I'm not alone, so I compiled a list of superhero movies for people who don't typically like superhero movies (franchise rule applies, one entry each). Let me know what you think, and please share your own opinions!

10: V for Vendetta - A sophisticated freedom fighter plots to overthrow a tyrannical government. The character "V" is smartly written and brilliantly portrayed by Hugo Weaving. Bonus points for Stephen Fry. I like it because it doesn't coddle the viewer; you have to bring a certain attitude with you to best enjoy this one.

9: Akira - A boy receives telekinetic powers and begins to lose control of his mind resulting in widespread chaos. The score here is one of the best in anime, and the animation holds up to this day. Akira is the film that convinced me that anime on blu-ray was worth it.

8: Dredd - The 2012 film reboot. I'm a big fan of films like this, where two powerful characters play cat and mouse, powers shift, and you really can't guess who will come out on top. Power struggles on a small scale, but worth it. Not the best movie in the world, but the concept is solid, and it's a breath of fresh air after the Stallone one.

7: Casshern - One of my favorite movies, superhero or otherwise. It's essentially the story of Dr. Light and Mega Man crossed with Batman, in Japan, fighting robots. Another "power struggle" movie where two formidable characters are constantly at odds. Brilliantly paced, and stunning fight choreography.

6: Hellboy - I could have included this one for the art direction alone, but there is so much goodness here. Ron Perlman delivers as Hellboy, and del Toro's direction is masterful. This is beginning to sound like a newsprint blurb. But seriously, this is a great flick.

5: Guardians of the Galaxy - Pretty much the only Marvel movie I give a crap about. Everyone says it but it's true, the soundtrack is amazing. Just the right mix of comedy and action, and there's that moment where Vin Diesel does that thing, and it's great. I don't have high hopes for the sequel though.

4: Sin City - This is your film noir entry. Amazing cinematography and direction. The digital effects are great, and I usually hate digital effects. Everything here is done very well, and Elijah Wood's performace is still one of my favorites in the world of comic book films. Not a "superhero" movie, really, but I'm putting this here as it is steeped in the culture.

3: The Dark Knight - I don't care about Batman. He is my least favorite popular superhero. The only time I gave a crap about Batman was in the Batman/Aliens crossover comic books, and even then I was rooting for the Aliens. But Heath Ledger's Joker? Well, that alone brings this movie to the forefront. Everyone knows that by now, so I'm sure this being on here is no surprise, but I had to include it. Another power struggle movie between two characters; I love that.

2: The Watchmen - This is your art house entry. This is all character development. The payoffs here are narrative ones and I wouldn't have it any other way. Set design, cinematography, and costuming are outstanding with this one. Probably the most "adult" movie on my list, even more-so than V for Vendetta. This takes that power struggle concept I like so much and explores it in a web of about five different relationships.

1: Unbreakable - If nobody tells you, you may not even know you're watching a superhero movie until about halfway through. This one put my cousin to sleep and he begged me to play something else, but the kid doesn't know what's good for him. M Night, sure, but back when he was good, more or less. My theme of conflict through power struggle is in full swing here with Samuel L. Jackson's Mr. Glass as the antagonist to a character that cannot be hurt. Great concept and great execution.
